title: Modules courbes elliptiques en caractéristiques ≠2 : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 75–78): Grothendieck is building a coordinate-free version of the Legendre normal form y^2 = x(x-1)(x-λ) for elliptic curves over a field k of characteristic ≠ 2. The data are:
- J, a 3-element set (the three nonzero 2-torsion points / finite branch points);
- Σ_J, the projective line canonically attached to J (P^1 with J as three marked points);
- t ∈ Σ_J^*(k), the 'λ' point;
- ω_J, a μ_2-torsor of 'orientations' attached to J;
- T_0, a line built from these data with T_0^{⊗2} ≅ T_{Σ,t} (12).

On the previous page a 'Legendre pinning' (épinglage de Legendre) is defined as a pair (α, κ):
- κ : T_{E,0} ≅ T_0 is an iso compatible with squares (14). There are exactly two, forming a μ_2-torsor; this is the usual sign ambiguity of the invariant differential dx/y.
- α : ω_J ≅ ∂Q_0 = Q_0{±1} is needed because ω_J is not yet fixed while J varies. Here Q_0 is an auxiliary 'square', a 4-element set with cyclic (dihedral) structure.

This page normalizes Q_0. If Q_0 is fixed once and for all, its two orientations form a μ_2-torsor ω_{Q_0}. Giving an orientation means identifying ω_{Q_0} with μ_4^* = {i, -i}, the primitive 4th roots of unity (16). Equivalently it means a section of the contracted product μ_4^* ∧^{μ_2} ω_{Q_0}, or an iso μ_4 ≅ Aut^+(Q_0) (17): the orientation picks out the generator 'rotation by +90°'.

The 'most natural' choice is to make Q_0 tautological. Fix a side of the square whose two consecutive vertices are labelled s_i, s_{i'} by the two square roots of -1. Impose s_{i'} = i·s_i (18), hence s_i = i'·s_{i'} since i' = i^{-1} = -i (both relations are consistent).

T_0 is then characterized by a structure on the twisted line T_0 ⊗ U_f(-1): a pair of basis vectors indexed by μ_4^* satisfying (18). The square Q_0 is then the μ_4-orbit {±s_i, ±s_{i'}} inside this line, and the product i·s_i is taken in its vector-space structure.

This yields a canonical iso D_{Q_0} ≅ μ_4^* (19). Hence datum (16) becomes, on the next page, α : ω_J ≅ μ_4^* (20). Elliptic curves with Legendre pinning are then equivalent to triples (J, t, α).

When J is identified with {0,1,∞} (Jacobi level-2 structure), ω_J has a privileged element ω^+. The datum α then reduces to the choice of a square root i of -1, the 'arithmetic' datum, and Legendre–Jacobi pinned curves form a rigid groupoid.

Purpose: this is the torsor bookkeeping that makes the Legendre form functorial in J, i.e. equivariant under S_3 = Aut(J). Classically, the substitutions λ ↦ 1-λ etc. only preserve the Legendre form up to a quadratic twist by -1. Grothendieck absorbs this by the μ_4^* torsor: a choice of √-1.
errors: No mathematical error: (18) is self-consistent since i' = i^{-1} = -i. The exact meaning of U_f(-1) and D_{Q_0} is not recoverable from this page alone. The sentence about 'the product i s_i' is only partly legible.

ideas.what: Rigidifying data for the Legendre form: level-2 structure plus a choice of invariant differential up to the μ_2 sign, with the λ-line as fine moduli
ideas.modern_name: Legendre moduli problem / Legendre structure (level 2 + differential)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Legendre, Jacobi); moduli formulation in Igusa, Deligne–Rapoport, Katz–Mazur (1985)

ideas.what: Encoding the √-1 ambiguity of the S_3-symmetry of the Legendre family as a μ_2-torsor iso ω_J ≅ μ_4^* (primitive 4th roots), realized via the orientations of a 'square' Q_0 and Aut^+(Q_0) ≅ μ_4
ideas.modern_name: Torsor/contracted-product bookkeeping; twisting of the Legendre family by -1 under λ ↦ 1-λ
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore (the quadratic twist by -1 in the S_3 action on Legendre curves is well known)

ideas.what: Tautological model of the square as the μ_4-orbit of a vector in a twisted line T_0 ⊗ U(-1), with vertices labelled by μ_4^*
ideas.modern_name: μ_4-torsor inside a line; canonical choice of base point

missed.claim: A fully canonical (choice-free in J) formulation of the Legendre pinning. In it the only 'arithmetic' input is a μ_2-torsor iso ω_J ≅ μ_4^*, which reduces to a choice of √-1 once J ≅ {0,1,∞}. This gives an S_3-equivariant Legendre family over the stack of 3-element sets, a cleaner bookkeeping than usually written. However, the underlying phenomenon (twist by -1, need for √-1 to make S_3 act) is known, so this is a nice presentation rather than a new result.
missed.quote: la donnée (16) équivaut : à la donnée d'une iso (20) α : ω_J ≃ μ_4^*
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It could serve as a clean model for Galois-equivariant (GT/anabelian) treatments of the Legendre family over P^1 - {0,1,∞}, where the S_3-action and the role of √-1 matter. It is marginal novelty.

deep.surprise_reason: This is careful torsor-theoretic bookkeeping of a classically known phenomenon (the Legendre form's S_3-symmetry requires √-1). It is elegant and characteristically Grothendieckian, but a specialist would not find new mathematics here.
transcription_corrections: Lines 2–3 likely read '..., on aura comme seule donnée une iso' rather than 'on aura aussi la donnée d'une iso'.
'avec un coté fixé, dont l'un des sommets consécutifs s, s' sont donc en corr. biunivoque avec les éléments de μ_4^* = {i, i'}' — 'l'un' should probably be 'les éléments'.
'Ainsi, T_0 peut s'interpréter comme muni de la structure suivante, qui la caractérise:' — 'comme une de la structure' should be 'comme muni de la structure'.
In (17) the left side appears as μ_4^* (with asterisk), matching (16).
'Ici on a une iso. canonique' — the word 'aussi' is doubtful.
Line before (19) reads roughly 'et maintenant le produit i s_i est ... au sens de la structure vectorielle de T_0 ⊗ U_f(-1)'.
